featured_reviews.name: Prashant Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was a very disappointing hospital experience. Despite having mediclaim, the hospital charged excessively for almost everything. The patient was admitted only to a general/semi-private ward and was not in the ICU for most of the stay, yet the final bill was extremely high.

They charge separately for even basic services such as nursing, RMO visits, oxygen, nebulization, biomedical waste, food, and repeated doctor visits. It feels more like a money-making system than a healthcare facility. The infrastructure and facilities are very poor and below standard, but the charges are comparable to premium hospitals.

Doctor visit fees were charged multiple times, pathology and medicine costs were highly inflated, and the overall management was very unprofessional. For the level of service and facilities provided, these charges are completely unjustified.

There are many much better hospitals in Mumbai with experienced doctors, cleaner wards, better patient care, and more reasonable billing, even for mediclaim patients. This hospital is especially not suitable for senior citizens.

I strongly do not recommend this hospital to anyone using mediclaim or paying out of pocket. There are many better and more ethical hospitals available
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Sir,

We regret that you feel dissatisfied with your experience. Please note that all charges are transparent and raised as per standard hospital protocols and mediclaim guidelines. Even in a general/semi-private ward, services such as nursing care, RMO monitoring, oxygen support, investigations, and doctor visits are billed separately based on medical necessity and documentation.

We assure you that there is no inflation in billing, and every charge can be explained in detail. We request you to kindly connect with our billing department so we can review your concerns personally.

Regards,
Team Radiant Hospital

featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Wairkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would like to share my experience with Prakruti Hospital in Virar West. My mother-in-law, Smita Sunil Sandim, had a gallbladder operation there. The surgery was performed by Dr. Yashodhar Mahimkar, who is an excellent surgeon. He explained everything very clearly and made sure we understood the entire process.

All the hospital staff are very supportive and caring. The operation was done through the Ayushman Bharat card and it was completely free. The hospital did not charge anything for the surgery.

The Ayushman Bharat process was also handled very quickly by the hospital staff, so we did not face any problems. The hospital is very clean and well maintained, which helps patients feel comfortable and safe.

The nurses and staff are very kind and explain everything properly to the patients and their families.

Thank you to Dr. Yashodhar Mahimkar and the entire Prakruti Hospital staff for their excellent care and support.

featured_reviews.name: Seyony Vinoj
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was the worst hospital experience my family has ever had. My husband was admitted here, and throughout his stay I felt that his condition deteriorated rather than improved. I was very disappointed with the level of care and communication we received.
I felt that financial concerns were given more importance than patient care, which added to our distress during an already difficult time. The ICU team's discussions about my husband's prognosis were upsetting and left me feeling hopeless.
Sadly, my husband passed away, and I am left with serious concerns about the care he received. Based on my experience, I would not recommend this hospital and would encourage others to carefully consider their options.

featured_reviews.name: Mustafa Indorewala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointing experience. The doctor may be knowledgeable, but limiting OPD consultations to only 5–6 patients per day makes it extremely difficult for patients to access medical care when they need it. Medical emergencies and health concerns do not always happen according to a schedule.
Many patients travel long distances expecting to be seen, only to find that no more patients are being accepted. There should be a better system to accommodate urgent cases or existing patients who require timely medical attention. Accessibility and patient care are just as important as medical expertise.
